# two_exponents
## Description
For some reason, Alice decided to publish two different exponents for the same modulus. We have a suspicion she encoded the same message twice. Can you show her why it's a bad idea to reuse the modulus in RSA?

```
N = 3033460252672479184149060571612607183221638086938515053929970323252159838745899671775328169188026170501264589184326481376335529234261876962970936222103129611620981298795931116654812119974128816322101710494071379984696571174131523402101217676162518053180451

e1 = 65537

c1 = 1039261459667825850045647190647616574037612197758842047642381807586907458738743977556491007175790501185425525084355026497164307618220702298350887104687454115667970452590471711458059703811925639755824782738709827459242752868902974091877325251926572895938503

e2 = 73559

c2 =  1206445849044810272920422376557912664512397119147378545737563096665988689013522279291080362091645219730340297905203544690702402400138869488839305247330829099155651010293259737907010703175480801382962111979681304702327373546014885081611447915305374171681803
```
## Solution
I googled "common modulus attack rsa" and found [this](https://crypto.stackexchange.com/questions/16283/how-to-use-common-modulus-attack) as the second result. The answer to that StackExchange question shows how the plaintext can be derived from the [extended Euclidean algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_Euclidean_algorithm), so I yoinked some code from [here](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/euclidean-algorithms-basic-and-extended/) and implemented the provided formula. Here's the script:
```python
from Crypto.Util.number import long_to_bytes

N = 3033460252672479184149060571612607183221638086938515053929970323252159838745899671775328169188026170501264589184326481376335529234261876962970936222103129611620981298795931116654812119974128816322101710494071379984696571174131523402101217676162518053180451
e1 = 65537
c1 = 1039261459667825850045647190647616574037612197758842047642381807586907458738743977556491007175790501185425525084355026497164307618220702298350887104687454115667970452590471711458059703811925639755824782738709827459242752868902974091877325251926572895938503
e2 = 73559
c2 =  1206445849044810272920422376557912664512397119147378545737563096665988689013522279291080362091645219730340297905203544690702402400138869488839305247330829099155651010293259737907010703175480801382962111979681304702327373546014885081611447915305374171681803

def extended_gcd(a, b): 
    if a == 0 :  
        return b, 0, 1
             
    gcd, x1, y1 = extended_gcd(b % a, a) 
     
    x = y1 - (b // a) * x1 
    y = x1 
     
    return gcd, x, y
      
_, s1, s2 = extended_gcd(e1, e2) 

m = (pow(c1, s1, N) * pow(c2, s2, N)) % N
print(long_to_bytes(m).decode())
```
Here's the flag: `gigem{see1ng_d0ub1e}`
